social_security.summary: Taxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits on the federal return are subtracted, so Georgia does not tax them.

sources.quote: Does Georgia tax Social Security? No. Taxable Social Security and Railroad Retirement on the Federal return are exempt from Georgia Income Tax. The taxable portion is subtracted on schedule 1 of Form 500.

public_pension.summary: Government pensions count as retirement income for Georgia's retirement income exclusion: up to $35,000 per person at ages 62-64 (or if totally and permanently disabled) and up to $65,000 at 65 or older; the rest is taxable.
conditions: Age 62-64 (or totally and permanently disabled): up to $35,000
Cap is per person; covers pensions, annuities, interest, dividends, rents, capital gains, royalties and a limited amount of earned income

sources.quote: Taxpayers who are 62 or older, or permanently and totally disabled regardless of age, may be eligible for a retirement income adjustment on their Georgia tax return. Retirement income includes: Income from pensions and annuities
Veterans ages 62 to 64 are eligible for Georgia's existing retirement income tax exemption for up to $35,000. Those over the age of 65 are eligible for an exemption of up to $65,000.
Retirement income exceeding the maximum adjustable amount will be taxed at the normal rate.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, annuities and IRA/401(k) distributions share the same retirement income exclusion: up to $35,000 at ages 62-64 and $65,000 at 65 or older; the rest is taxable.
conditions: Age 62-64 (or totally and permanently disabled): up to $35,000
Shared cap with other retirement income

sources.quote: A retirement exclusion is allowed provided the taxpayer is 62 years of age or older, or the taxpayer is totally and permanently disabled. Retirement income includes items such as: interest, dividends, net rentals, capital gains, royalties, pensions, annuities
Veterans ages 62 to 64 are eligible for Georgia's existing retirement income tax exemption for up to $35,000. Those over the age of 65 are eligible for an exemption of up to $65,000.

military_retirement.summary: Military retirees under 62 may exclude up to $17,500 of military retirement income, plus another $17,500 if they have more than $17,500 of Georgia earned income; at 62 or older the general $35,000/$65,000 retirement exclusion applies.
conditions: Under 62 with more than $17,500 of Georgia earned income: additional $17,500

sources.quote: Beginning January 1, 2022, $17,500 of military retirement income can be excluded for taxpayers under 62 years of age and an additional $17,500 can be excluded for taxpayers with more than $17,500 of earned income in Georgia.
Veterans who retired from the military and are under 62 years of age are eligible for an exemption of up to $17,500 of military retirement income.

notes: lexflow has no Georgia statute index, so there are no statute sources (the rules are in O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(5)). The $35,000/$65,000 caps are not stated on the Department of Revenue's HTML pages (they refer to the IT-511 booklet, a PDF lexflow cannot read here), so they are grounded on the Georgia Department of Veterans Service page. DOR's 'Retirees - FAQ' still says the exclusion covers 'the first $4000.00 of earned income', while DOR's 'Retirement Income Exclusion' page says 'Up to $5,000 of earned income'; the $5,000 figure is the newer one.
